Here’s a comprehensive overview of Francis Ngannou, accurate as of mid-2024. Combat sports move quickly, so for events after this date, I recommend checking recent official sources.

### 🔹 Basic Information
- **Full Name**: Francis Ngannou
- **Born**: February 5, 1986, in Batié, Cameroon
- **Nationality**: Cameroonian-French
- **Height**: 6 ft 4 in (193 cm)
- **Reach**: 83 in (211 cm)
- **Weight Class**: Heavyweight
- **Stance**: Orthodox
- **Professional MMA Record**: 17–3 (12 KOs, 1 submission, 4 decisions)

---

### 🌍 Early Life & Background
Ngannou grew up in extreme poverty in rural Cameroon. As a teenager, he worked in sand mines to support his family and had little formal education. Inspired by Mike Tyson and driven by a desire to escape poverty, he began training in boxing and martial arts locally. At age 26, he left Cameroon for France with almost no money, enduring homelessness and odd jobs while training at the MMA Factory in Paris. His work ethic, coachability, and raw athleticism quickly set him apart.

---

### 🥊 MMA Career
#### UFC Rise (2015–2023)
- **UFC Debut**: December 2015, defeated Luis Henrique by TKO.
- Gained notoriety for a string of devastating first-round knockouts, including wins over Andrei Arlovski, Anthony Hamilton, and Alistair Overeem.
- **First Title Shot**: Lost to Stipe Miocic by unanimous decision at UFC 220 (Jan 2018). Exposed grappling deficiencies but showed championship heart.
- **Redemption & Title Win**: Rematched Miocic at **UFC 260** (Mar 2021), winning by TKO in round 2 to become **UFC Heavyweight Champion**.
- **Title Defense**: Defeated Ciryl Gane by unanimous decision at **UFC 270** (Jan 2022), showcasing vastly improved wrestling and fight IQ.
- **Departure**: Despite being champion, Ngannou was stripped of the title in January 2023 after contract negotiations broke down. Key sticking points included fighter pay, health insurance, sponsorship freedom, and the right to pursue professional boxing.

#### Fighting Style
Known as one of the hardest punchers in MMA history, Ngannou combines elite knockout power with improving wrestling, clinch work, and fight IQ. His athletic explosiveness, reach, and cardio improvements transformed him from a raw striker into a well-rounded heavyweight champion.

---

### 🥊 Professional Boxing Career
Ngannou transitioned to boxing while still an active MMA fighter, leveraging his power and athleticism:
- **vs. Tyson Fury** (Oct 28, 2023): Made his pro boxing debut against the undefeated WBC heavyweight champion. Ngannou knocked Fury down in round 3 and lost a highly competitive split decision. The performance earned widespread acclaim and shattered expectations.
- **vs. Anthony Joshua** (Mar 8, 2024): Fought former unified heavyweight champion in Riyadh. Ngannou was knocked out in round 2 after a competitive first round. The fight was part of a major Middle East boxing card and further raised his global profile.

His boxing record stands at **0–2**, but both fights were against elite, former/active world champions, and his performances significantly elevated his marketability and respect in combat sports.

---

### 🤝 PFL Era & Business Ventures
- In **May 2023**, Ngannou signed a landmark deal with the **Professional Fighters League (PFL)**.
- The contract is widely considered fighter-friendly: it includes equity ownership, freedom to box, no exclusive fight mandates, and a role as **Chairman of PFL Africa**, aimed at developing MMA across the continent.
- He competes in the PFL's "Super Fights" division, which features high-profile, non-tournament matchups with flexible scheduling.
- His signing is viewed as a milestone for fighter empowerment and league competition in MMA.

---

### ❤️ Personal Life & Philanthropy
- Married to **Denise Zoung** in 2023. The couple keeps much of their personal life private.
- Fluent in French, English, and several Cameroonian languages.
- Founded the **Francis Ngannou Foundation**, which focuses on providing sports training, education, and mentorship to underprivileged youth in Cameroon and across Africa.
- Known for his humility, discipline, and advocacy for fighter rights, healthcare, and fair compensation in combat sports.

---

### 🏆 Legacy & Impact
- One of the most devastating heavyweights in MMA history, with a highlight reel of one-punch knockouts.
- Symbol of upward mobility: from sand mines in Cameroon to global champion and sports entrepreneur.
- Pivotal figure in the modern fighter rights movement, challenging traditional promotional models and pushing for better conditions, cross-sport freedom, and athlete ownership.
- Inspired a new generation of African fighters and helped put Cameroonian and continental MMA on the global map.

---

### 📅 Current Status (as of mid-2024)
- Active in the PFL with anticipated super fights.
- Continuing selective boxing matches against top-tier opposition.
- Expanding PFL Africa and his foundation's outreach programs.
- Remains one of the most recognizable and influential figures in global combat sports.

If you'd like details on a specific fight, contract terms, training camp, or his foundation's work, let me know and I can dive deeper.
